fixer.title: mcp: fix local gateway disposal

introducer.title: mcp: initial data flow for MCP gateway

cases.mechanism: Each local gateway disposal previously sent `[gatewayId]` to a channel expecting `gatewayId`, causing cleanup to miss every string-keyed entry. One route and its event/session state remained per configured MCP server, and the HTTP listener could remain open until client disconnect or process shutdown; repeated create/dispose cycles accumulated this retained state.
cases.symptom: Disposed local gateways retained per-server routes, sessions and event listeners and continued processing server-change events; the gateway HTTP server also remained alive when these leaked routes were the last routes.
cases.fixedBehavior: The changed line calls the channel directly with the scalar gateway ID expected by McpGatewayChannel, allowing it to dispose the per-gateway event forwarder, remove client tracking, clean all per-server routes and sessions/listeners, and stop the shared HTTP server when the last route is gone.
cases.evidence: The base line invokes disposeGateway through ProxyChannel.toService. ProxyChannel.toService sends method arguments as an array (`channel.call(propKey, methodArgs)`), while McpGatewayChannel's manual `call` implementation casts its raw `args` to `string`. The resulting one-element array does not equal the string key used by `_gatewayDisposables`, `_clientGateways`, or McpGatewayService's `_gatewayRoutes`, so the service returns as an unknown gateway without running `_cleanupGateway`. The extension-host API reaches this path whenever a locally created McpGateway is disposed, via ExtHostMcp.dispose -> MainThreadMcp.$disposeMcpGateway -> result.dispose.

fixer.title: Refine chat session indicators and add topology telemetry

introducer.title: POC: Chat session state frames

cases.mechanism: An infinite CSS animation changed a large blurred box-shadow on a pseudo-element covering the entire chat widget while each request was in progress, forcing continuous rendering/paint work until completion.
cases.symptom: Sustained CPU/GPU paint load and potential dropped frames while a chat request runs, especially for large chat editor surfaces or multiple simultaneously visible sessions.
cases.fixedBehavior: In-progress sessions no longer create or animate the full-widget pseudo-element; only static idle-unvisited and needs-input frames remain, eliminating the continuous large-area box-shadow repaint during long-running requests.
cases.evidence: The base CSS applies `animation: chat-session-working-glow 1.4s ease-in-out infinite` to the full-widget `.interactive-session.chat-state-in-progress::before` overlay. The keyframes animate `box-shadow` from spacing-size20 to spacing-size60, so every active chat request continuously repaints a large blurred region for the request lifetime. This PR deletes both the in-progress pseudo-element selector and the infinite box-shadow animation, while `ChatWidget.updateSessionStateIndicator` still transitions request state normally.

fixer.title: chat: fix GitHub context repository selection

introducer.title: Harden content exclusion failrue condition

cases.mechanism: Folder-based GitHub context resolution previously called getRepositoryFetchUrls, which eagerly awaited the shared initial Git repository discovery before reading remotes; that wait is bounded only after 30 seconds and discovery itself waits for every repository HEAD to initialize.
cases.symptom: Opening the Issue or Pull Request context picker for a selected local folder could be blocked for up to 30 seconds when local Git HEAD metadata remained unresolved.
cases.fixedBehavior: The new local repository-root fast path reads `.git/config` (including worktree pointers) and returns remote URLs before waitForInitialDiscovery, so the picker can proceed without waiting for HEAD/discovery.
cases.evidence: The changed Agents-window path passes its single local folder URI to the extension command; resolveGitHubContextRepository calls getRepositoryFetchUrls. RIGHT lines 200-216 now read and return direct config before the still-existing wait at line 226. waitForInitialDiscovery shares a raceTimeout with INITIAL_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS=30,000, while initial discovery waits for every repository HEAD. The added unresolved-metadata tests exercise the URI pass-through path. Base blame identifies commit 88a8ef6f793d1b593b47862bd00aab36e88b0733 as introducing the old wait on base line 202.

fixer.title: sessions: measure and unblock V3 onboarding GitHub personalization

introducer.title: Add prompt options to V3 onboarding

cases.mechanism: Initial prompt-option rendering was serialized behind repository discovery and multiple GitHub GraphQL stages, with up to the full 10-second total timeout on the onboarding critical path.
cases.symptom: The onboarding widget remained in loading skeletons for seconds or timed out before presenting usable options; experiment telemetry cited in the PR observed 61% timeout impressions with zero GitHub options.
cases.fixedBehavior: The runner now sends a complete standard three-option state through the progress callback before awaiting GitHub personalization, then incrementally refines slots. GitHub work remains asynchronous and no longer blocks first usable prompt-option paint.
cases.evidence: In the base implementation, `_runPromptOptions` displayed loading skeletons and awaited `resolveOptions(token)` before calling `showPromptOptions(state)`. `resolveOptions` awaited repository resolution plus concurrent issue and PR chains; the PR chain could sequentially consume the 5s summary and 4s review budgets under the 10s total timeout. The changed line publishes the three standard options synchronously before entering that lookup, so first usable paint no longer waits for filesystem/GitHub boundaries. The PR reports the affected experiment had 61% zero-GitHub-option timeouts and a tour-reach deficit, matching this call-path mechanism.

fixer.title: agentHost: centralize session and chat catalog metadata

introducer.title: agentHost: make the orchestrator own session enumeration and chat lifecycle

cases.mechanism: Every list computation opened each visible session's separate SQLite database and read a broad metadata object, creating filesystem/SQLite fan-out proportional to the catalog size even when entries were unchanged.
cases.symptom: The old code explicitly described catalog listing as slow because it opened every registered session database and emitted slow-list timing when this path exceeded the threshold.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added catalog-reader call serves eligible rows from the central `sessions_v2` database and only sends missing, stale, or invalid rows through the legacy per-session fallback, removing steady-state per-session database opens.
cases.evidence: The deleted overlay mapped every listed session through `tryOpenDatabase(s.session)` and `getMetadataObject(...)`; the added path at line 2794 reads the central catalog projection under concurrency 4, returns eligible metadata directly, and reserves `_legacyRegisteredSessionMetadata` for ineligible rows. The base line carrying the unconditional per-session open blames to the supplied introducing commit.

fixer.title: startup: Cache packaged ESM ASAR resolutions

introducer.title: Use synchronous hooks for ESM ASAR resolution

cases.mechanism: Repeated imports of the same packaged bare module synchronously repeated default resolution and ASAR package/direct resolution instead of reusing the prior successful result.
cases.symptom: Repeated synchronous module and ASAR resolution consumed main-process CPU during packaged startup and later repeated dynamic imports.
cases.fixedBehavior: The hook keys successful archive resolutions by specifier, normalized parent path, conditions, and import attributes, then returns the cached resolver output before invoking the default resolver or ASAR lookup. It leaves failures, closer dependencies, external parents, CommonJS, and non-packaged processes uncached.
cases.evidence: Before this PR, every packaged ESM bare-specifier resolution that missed the default resolver reached synchronous ASAR resolution (`asarRequire.resolve`) even when the same specifier and parent had already resolved. The added integration test invokes four resolutions for two effective specifier-parent contexts and proves the changed hook performs only two archive package lookups plus two cache hits; without the added cache lookup/set, all four invocations follow the old archive-resolution path. `bootstrap-esm.ts` is imported by packaged Electron main/fork/CLI entry points, placing this repeated synchronous resolver work on startup and later dynamic-import paths.

fixer.title: configuration: batch initial policy definitions

introducer.title: check for valid account and provide option to sign in

cases.mechanism: Two sequential definition batches each changed the accumulated policy definitions, causing the backend to perform collection-wide policy initialization twice; native desktop recreated the policy watcher after the first batch and blocked startup on the second watcher creation.
cases.symptom: Configuration/policy initialization occupied the startup critical path and delayed main-process I/O callbacks; measured policy initialization improved by 12 ms after batching, with related callbacks improving by 8-10 ms.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added array union at configurations.ts:125 submits regular and excluded configuration keys to one `updatePolicyDefinitions` call, so the abstract service performs one backend update and native watcher construction (or one file-policy refresh) instead of two sequential updates during configuration startup.
cases.evidence: Base `PolicyConfiguration.initialize()` invoked `updatePolicyDefinitions` once for default keys and awaited it before invoking it again for excluded keys. `AbstractPolicyService.updatePolicyDefinitions` calls `_updatePolicyDefinitions(this.policyDefinitions)` whenever each batch adds definitions; on Windows/macOS `NativePolicyService._updatePolicyDefinitions` dynamically imports `@vscode/policy-watcher`, queues creation, and replaces its `MutableDisposable<Watcher>`, while Linux `FilePolicyService` rereads and parses the policy file. This initialization is awaited by `ConfigurationService.initialize()` and the workbench/session initialization path. The PR's instrumented startup data reports that eliminating the second batch removes one watcher build and reduces the blocking policy initialization segment by 8-12 ms.

fixer.title: Recognize eagerness option in PatchBased02Unified

introducer.title: nes: let settings and experiments override baked strategy values

cases.mechanism: The newly introduced unified strategy was not classified as an eagerness-aware prompt, so every qualifying inline-edit request redundantly installed an artificial post-response latency gate before yielding the first edit.
cases.symptom: Users selecting explicit Medium or Low eagerness with PatchBased02Unified could wait until 700 ms or 1500 ms total request time before the first edit was displayed even when the model response was ready sooner.
cases.fixedBehavior: Adding PatchBased02Unified to isEagernessPrompt recognizes that the model already receives eagerness through its prompt and skips the redundant client timing override, removing up to 700 ms (Medium) or 1500 ms (Low) from first-edit presentation without changing prompt construction or network request cardinality.
cases.evidence: Commit ee9c82e739d0b52261d9804317f83d14f71429aa introduced PatchBased02Unified, but the base isEagernessPrompt whitelist omitted it. Model configuration preserves eagernessPrompt in overrideModelConfig, promptCrafting already emits the aggression tag for PatchBased02Unified, and _configureDebounceTimings calls _applyAggressivenessSettings whenever isEagernessPrompt is false. For explicit Medium/Low settings that path sets DelaySession.expectedTotalTime to the 700/1500 ms defaults, and stream parsing awaits the remaining artificial delay before yielding the first edit.

fixer.title: agentHost: centralize session and chat catalog metadata

introducer.title: agentHost: make the orchestrator own session enumeration and chat lifecycle

cases.mechanism: The prior listSessions overlay opened every visible session's separate session.db and read its metadata, after provider metadata enumeration, so list latency scaled with the number of databases and provider sessions.
cases.symptom: PR measurements show the old path taking about 1.3 seconds cold and 432 ms warm for 26 sessions.
cases.fixedBehavior: Verified rows are now read from the central agent-host.db payload and only missing/invalid rows fall back to provider and per-session database reads.
cases.evidence: The deleted _computeSessions path used a per-session limiter and tryOpenDatabase/getMetadataObject for every listed row; added line 2817 reads the central catalog representation. The PR's equivalent-profile measurements show cold mean falling from 1314.9 ms to 123.4 ms and warm mean from 431.6 ms to 80.0 ms. Base blame resolves the old per-session path to the introducing commit.

fixer.title: Add transient UI for /btw side questions

introducer.title: agentHost: add session and chat rename tools

cases.mechanism: Every outgoing side-chat turn synchronously joined the title contribution's async persisted-metadata database lookup before the turn could be sent.
cases.symptom: Side-chat send startup incurred an avoidable serialized database open/metadata read on each turn.
cases.fixedBehavior: Side-chat turns now return before the persisted-title metadata lookup and therefore do not block send startup on that database read or add the rename reminder to the turn.
cases.evidence: Before this change, SessionTitleContribution.onOutgoingTurn awaited prepareInstructionForAgent for every outgoing Agent Host turn, and the contribution dispatcher awaits each contribution serially before sending. For an independent side chat, prepareInstructionForAgent reached _readPersistedTitleMetadata, which awaits sessionDataService.tryOpenDatabase and ref.object.getMetadata. The added SideChat-origin guard at line 519 returns before that storage access. blame_base_line attributes the old await to 274239ff17a15514f74288e0f8fb21eaccce599b.

fixer.title: nes: Recognize eagerness option in PatchBased02Unified

introducer.title: nes: let settings and experiments override baked strategy values

cases.mechanism: PatchBased02Unified eagerness requests were misclassified, redundantly applying a generic debounce or minimum-response delay on every invocation and holding the first visible edit.
cases.symptom: Inline edit suggestions could be artificially delayed to 700 ms at Medium aggressiveness or 1500 ms at Low aggressiveness before the first edit was shown.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added strategy classification skips the redundant generic aggressiveness timing policy for PatchBased02Unified eagerness requests, allowing the HTTP request and first streamed edit to follow the strategy's baked latency settings rather than being held to the generic 700/1500 ms targets.
cases.evidence: Base line 548 introduced PatchBased02Unified. Its model configuration accepts eagernessPrompt and its prompt path emits an aggression tag, but before this change isEagernessPrompt omitted the strategy. Therefore xtabProvider._configureDebounceTimings invoked _applyAggressivenessSettings for each non-speculative inline-edit request. Low and Medium set DelaySession.expectedTotalTime to configured defaults of 1500 ms and 700 ms, and stream processing explicitly waits out the remaining artificial delay before yielding the first edit.

fixer.title: agentHost: centralize session and chat catalog metadata

introducer.title: agentHost: make the orchestrator own session enumeration and chat lifecycle

cases.mechanism: Each list computation scaled across all visible sessions with provider metadata retrieval followed by opening and querying every session.db, placing O(number of sessions) filesystem and SQLite boundaries on the list critical path.
cases.symptom: Large session catalogs produced slow cold and warm `listSessions` calls; the base code explicitly classified the all-session database pass as slow, and equivalent-profile measurements show roughly 1.3s cold mean and 432ms warm mean before the fix.
cases.fixedBehavior: Normal warm and migrated listings read one verified payload per visible registration from the central `agent-host.db`; provider metadata prewarming and per-session database opens now occur only for ineligible central rows, so the expensive filesystem/SQLite fan-out is removed from the steady-state list critical path.
cases.evidence: In the base `_computeSessions`, every visible registered session went through provider metadata work and then a second `overlayLimiter` pass that called `tryOpenDatabase(s.session)` and read a broad metadata object; the base comments identify provider reads as the dominant cost on a large catalogue and state that a catalog pass opens every registered database. The changed `_computeSessions` at line 2839 instead calls `AgentHostCatalogListReader.read`, whose only normal-path boundary is `AgentHostDatabase.getSessionV2` in the already-open central SQLite database; only missing/stale rows take `_legacyRegisteredSessionMetadata`. PR measurements corroborate the traced mechanism with cold mean 1314.9ms to 123.4ms and warm mean 431.6ms to 80.0ms.

fixer.title: ci: Reduce test runner startup overhead

introducer.title: Add JUnit reporter for unit tests

cases.mechanism: The CI Browser unit runner attached Mocha's verbose Spec reporter in addition to the JUnit reporter, serializing and writing full suite/test descriptions to the captured console for every test result.
cases.symptom: A representative 2,700-test Browser subset produced 2,761 console lines and 177 KB of captured output, adding unnecessary CI logging and ingestion work.
cases.fixedBehavior: Browser CI now emits compact dot progress to stdout while preserving the full JUnit artifact, reducing per-test console serialization and log ingestion volume.
cases.evidence: The changed CI-only branch replaces Mocha's Spec console reporter at test/unit/browser/index.js:94 with Dot while leaving MochaJUnitReporter attached immediately below, so detailed test results remain in JUnit. The Browser unit workflows invoke this branch with --tfs. Spec serializes suite and test titles for each result; the PR's same-2,700-test comparison records 2,761 lines/177 KB before versus 263 lines/80 KB with Dot, directly tying the old reporter to repeated CI log output.

fixer.title: Add transient UI for /btw side questions

introducer.title: agentHost: add session and chat rename tools

cases.mechanism: Active-agent title handling put an awaited session-database metadata read and a mandatory rename_chat tool instruction on outgoing turns for independent side chats, adding I/O and an avoidable tool round-trip before the side answer could settle.
cases.symptom: Agent Host side questions incurred unnecessary response latency from title metadata lookup and automatic rename-tool execution even though these transient side chats do not need a rename reminder.
cases.fixedBehavior: Side-chat turns now return before persisted title metadata I/O and before injecting the mandatory rename_chat instruction, removing the unnecessary database read and rename tool/agent continuation from each eligible side-chat response path.
cases.evidence: SessionTitleContribution.onOutgoingTurn synchronously awaits prepareInstructionForAgent on every outgoing Agent Host turn. In the base revision, eligible independent chats then awaited _readPersistedTitleMetadata, which opens the session database and reads metadata, and could return CHAT_RENAME_REMINDER, an instruction explicitly requiring the agent to invoke rename_chat. The added SideChat-origin guard at RIGHT line 519 exits before both operations; the added test seeds an automatic side-chat title and verifies the outgoing instruction is now undefined. blame_base_line attributes the old metadata/reminder path to 274239ff17a15514f74288e0f8fb21eaccce599b.

fixer.title: automations: fix: honor worktree and provider session configuration

introducer.title: Unify worktree isolation across agents

cases.mechanism: For host-generated worktree session IDs, the old code could not mark isolation pending before Codex createChat scheduled an eager prewarm. Codex then materialized a thread in the source checkout; first send had to await that stale materialization, unsubscribe it, and materialize again in the new worktree.
cases.symptom: Worktree-backed Codex sessions with host-generated IDs performed a wasted prewarm and could delay the first turn while the stale thread was cleaned up and recreated.
cases.fixedBehavior: The host now mints the session URI before provider creation and marks that exact ID pending, so Codex's prewarm guard sees it and skips eager materialization until the worktree working directory is finalized.
cases.evidence: The changed `_createProviderSession` now computes `session` and calls `notePending` before `provider.chats.createChat`. Codex `_createChat` calls `_schedulePrewarm`, whose pending check suppresses `_materializeIfNeeded`; without it, `_adoptWorkingDirectoryBeforeSend` awaits and unsubscribes the stale prewarm before changing cwd. The expanded test proves both client- and host-generated IDs are pending during provider creation. Blame attributes the old conditional pending-ID logic to the supplied introducing commit.

fixer.title: authentication: release provider activation listeners

introducer.title: fix: race activateByEvent with provider registration to prevent auth deadlock

cases.mechanism: Timed-out provider activation attempts leave raceCancellation promises pending and retain one cancellation listener on the AuthenticationService lifetime token per attempt until service shutdown.
cases.symptom: Repeated requests for unavailable authentication providers accumulate listeners and retained promise closures for the lifetime of the workbench, eventually triggering listener-leak warnings and increasing memory/dispatch work.
cases.fixedBehavior: Each activation attempt now owns a linked CancellationTokenSource whose dispose(true) runs from tryActivateProvider's finally block. Successful registration, activation failure, and the 5-second timeout all cancel the operation token and remove the registrations from the long-lived service token, bounding retained listeners to currently active attempts.
cases.evidence: Before this change, tryActivateProvider passed the AuthenticationService lifetime token directly to raceCancellation. raceCancellation registers token.onCancellationRequested and disposes that registration only when its input promise settles or the token is cancelled. On the 5-second missing-provider timeout, Event.toPromise is disposed without settling, so providerRegistered remains pending and its cancellation listener remains attached until the whole service is disposed. getSessions/createSession and the declared-provider scan can invoke this path repeatedly; the added regression test exercises repeated missing-provider timeouts and verifies that listener-leak warnings no longer occur. The changed lines create a child source linked to the service token and register dispose(true) in the operation store, so finally cancellation settles raceCancellation and removes both its listener and the child source's parent listener.

fixer.title: agentHost: Exclude SDK-native skills from directory discovery

introducer.title: Use Copilot SDK APIs to discover customizations

cases.mechanism: SDK-native plugin customizations were treated as directory-backed items even though their paths were outside all SDK discovery directories, causing the fallback invariant error to be emitted once per such customization on every discovery refresh.
cases.symptom: The PR records a recent session emitting the invariant error tens of thousands of times, creating excessive logging work and log I/O during customization refreshes.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added source check diverts plugin-owned agents into plugin projection instead of directory conversion (with corresponding checks for rules and skills), so these SDK-native items no longer hit the per-customization fallback error path; the remaining fallback diagnostic is also lowered from error to trace.
cases.evidence: Before the change, discoverAgents/rules/skills returned plugin-owned children to toDirectoryCustomizations; when no discovery directory contained them, base line 875 logged an error inside the per-customization loop. Added line 639 identifies plugin agents before insertion, corresponding added source checks handle rules and skills, and the new plugin projection keeps them out of that fallback path. blame identifies the SDK-discovery change that introduced the old mechanism.

fixer.title: Avoid synchronous activity bar size measurement

introducer.title: Support activity bar on top of primary side bar

cases.mechanism: A clientHeight geometry read of the rendered global action container ran synchronously inside every vertical Activity Bar layout, including the startup grid layout, and could flush pending style/layout work on the UI thread.
cases.symptom: Main-thread startup and resize layout latency from synchronous browser style/layout resolution in ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout.
cases.fixedBehavior: Vertical Activity Bar layout computes reserved global-action height from the two-action in-memory count and static action height/gap inputs, avoiding the synchronous DOM geometry read during startup and later layouts while retaining a single arithmetic calculation per layout.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout synchronously read globalCompositeBar.element.clientHeight on every vertical layout. Workbench layout constructs the Activity Bar as a grid leaf and workbenchGrid.layout invokes part layout on startup; ActivitybarPart.layout then calls ActivityBarCompositeBar.layout. The global action bar has already appended rendered action DOM, so this geometry read sits on the synchronous main-thread startup/layout path and can require style/layout resolution. The changed code replaces that read with GlobalCompositeBar.getHeight(actionHeight, actionGap), which uses the in-memory ActionBar length and the same sizing values published to CSS. Tests explicitly install a throwing clientHeight getter and verify all supported size/gap combinations, corroborating that the DOM measurement is no longer reached.

fixer.title: chat: reduce picker layout measurement work

introducer.title: chat input: refactor and responsiveness

cases.mechanism: The responsive chat picker layout sorted items by repeatedly reading live DOM geometry in the comparator and then reread every item's geometry for fit checks, multiplying synchronous layout-sensitive reads on startup, resize, and picker-content mutations.
cases.symptom: Excessive synchronous DOM measurement increased responsive picker layout latency; profiling/benchmark evidence in the reviewed change shows lower layout counts and per-call time after snapshotting bounds.
cases.fixedBehavior: The new _getVisibleItemBounds snapshots each connected visible picker's bounds once per check and sorts those snapshots, removing O(n log n) repeated synchronous geometry reads from comparator execution while preserving visual ordering.
cases.evidence: On chat input construction and every ResizeObserver/MutationObserver-triggered layout, layout() orders visible picker items and repeatedly calls _fitsAvailableWidth while compacting. In the base revision, _getOrderedVisibleItems filtered with getClientRects(), then its sort comparator called getBoundingClientRect() for both operands on every comparison; _fitsAvailableWidth subsequently measured every item again. The changed helper records one DOMRect per visible item and all ordering/fit checks reuse that snapshot. The added tests cover right-to-left/reverse ordering and hidden items, while the PR's measured scenario reports reduced Chromium layout count on three-picker narrow/resizing paths.

fixer.title: Overlap macOS signing and notarization in official builds

introducer.title: Sign macOS server binaries

cases.mechanism: A global phase barrier serialized the start of every ESRP notarization behind completion of the slowest signing subprocess, leaving already-signed artifacts idle and making step latency max(all signing durations) plus max(all notarization durations) rather than the maximum per-artifact sign/notarize chain.
cases.symptom: Official macOS build completion was delayed whenever artifact signing durations differed, because notarization for early-finished artifacts could not overlap the remaining signing work.
cases.fixedBehavior: Each artifact now forms an independent sign-then-notarize chain, so a completed artifact enters the external notarization operation immediately instead of idling behind the slowest unrelated signing job. The total boundary-call count remains four operations for universal builds or eight for architecture-specific builds, and effective concurrency remains bounded by the two or four artifact chains.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, all 2 (universal) or 4 (architecture-specific) sign-darwin subprocesses were started, then every signing result was awaited through line 47 before the first notarize-darwin subprocess could be spawned at line 51. Each subprocess invokes the synchronous dotnet ESRP CLI path in build/azure-pipelines/common/sign.ts, and the encompassing Azure Pipelines Codesign & Notarize step cannot complete until all operations finish. The changed helper awaits only the matching artifact's signing operation before starting its notarization, and Promise.all retains parallel processing across independent artifacts.

fixer.title: sessions: address #335583 review feedback on ActionList hover panels

introducer.title: Agents: support multiple pull requests per session

cases.mechanism: Unconditional per-session CI polling kept every inactive open draft PR on a 60-second network refresh loop, so background request volume scaled with the number of distinct inactive draft PRs tracked by the sessions contribution.
cases.symptom: Continuous GitHub check-runs API traffic and associated response processing for inactive draft sessions whose CI status was not being displayed.
cases.fixedBehavior: For an open draft PR, the contribution still performs one initial status refresh, but it registers the 60-second CI poller only while that draft's session is active. Inactive draft models therefore stop generating recurring GitHub check-runs requests, while non-drafts retain the previous polling behavior. Shared model references and refresh-promise coalescing preserve deduplication for duplicate keys and simultaneous refreshes.
cases.evidence: Base line 288 unconditionally registered GitHubPullRequestCIModel.startPolling() for every open PR after the status autorun acquired its CI model. GitHubPullRequestCIModel schedules one refresh every 60 seconds, and each refresh reaches GitHubPRCIFetcher.getCheckRuns(), which issues a GET to /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs. The contribution iterates every tracked session and PR identity, so inactive draft sessions generated one recurring request per distinct draft PR. The changed draft branch now observes active-session state and only owns startPolling() while that session is active; the added test proves inactive drafts receive the one initial refresh but zero polling registrations.

fixer.title: Batch SVG whitespace markers in the editor per line

introducer.title: Add a new rendering technique for whitespace

cases.mechanism: The default SVG whitespace renderer created one SVG child element for every visible space or tab. Overlay line replacement on scrolling and selection-related rendering repeatedly constructed and destroyed a DOM subtree whose node count scaled with visible whitespace glyphs rather than visible lines.
cases.symptom: Editors with renderWhitespace enabled and whitespace-dense visible lines incurred excessive synchronous DOM/style recalculation during scrolling and drag selection, causing increased renderer task time and frame delays.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added wrapper at whitespace.ts:234 emits the accumulated glyph geometry as a single SVG path per line, while _renderCircle and _renderArrow now return closed path-data subpaths. Rendering still scans and serializes each visible marker, but DOM element creation, attachment, style matching, and teardown shrink from one shape per whitespace glyph to at most one shape per rendered line.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, whitespace.ts:219 appends a separate <circle> for each visible space, while _renderArrow returns a separate <path> for each visible tab. _applyRenderWhitespace iterates every whitespace character of every visible line (bounded by stopRenderingLineAfter, whose default is 10,000), and SVG is the default experimentalWhitespaceRendering mode. ViewOverlays.prepareRender runs the overlay on invalidation, ViewOverlayLine concatenates its markup with the other overlays, and viewLayer applies changed line HTML through innerHTML, making all of those glyph nodes synchronous DOM/style work during visible-line rendering. The PR body provides controlled editor measurements showing 778 glyph elements before versus 49 per-line paths after and corresponding reductions in selection and scrolling style-recalculation time.

fixer.title: Reuse text buffers in chat edits for checkpoint replay

introducer.title: refactor: edit operations timeline

cases.mechanism: Checkpoint replay rebuilt and reserialized the entire text buffer for every recorded text-edit operation, producing O(K*N)-style full-document CPU/allocation work for K small batches over a large file and blocking undo, redo, restore, and cold snapshot/diff model creation.
cases.symptom: Large chat-edited files with many recorded edit operations can freeze or substantially delay checkpoint undo/redo/restore and cold historical diff rendering because repeated full-document scans and copies execute before those actions complete.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added contiguous TextEdit grouping applies all version-ordered edit batches to one PieceTreeTextBuffer and extracts content only once per ordinary-text run, reducing full-buffer construction/extraction from one per edit operation to one per run while retaining create/delete/rename and notebook boundaries and disposing the buffer in finally.
cases.evidence: Before this PR, _replayOperations awaited _applyOperationToState once for every TextEdit operation; that branch called _applyTextEditsToContent for each operation. _applyTextEditsToContent calls createTextBuffer on the complete current content, whose createTextBufferFactory passes the entire string to PieceTreeTextBufferBuilder.acceptChunk/createLineStarts, and then extracts the complete resulting string. The path is directly awaited by undoInteraction/redoInteraction/restoreSnapshot through navigateToCheckpoint, and by snapshot-model creation used for diff rendering. Thus K edit batches over a document of size N repeatedly scan and materialize the full document on the renderer-side critical path. The PR's tests also establish the old multiplicity versus the fixed invariant by asserting one buffer creation/disposal for multiple edit operations.

fixer.title: sessions: Fix connection diagnostics focus and lifecycle

introducer.title: Mobile chat (1/10): infra primitives — bottom sheet body, visualViewport, longPress, pulldown, edge-swipe

cases.mechanism: Closing or unregistering an auxiliary window bypassed the sheet's sole close path, leaving the sheet DisposableStore, rendered DOM/body state, caller closures, and unresolved promise reachable for the remaining workbench lifetime.
cases.symptom: Auxiliary-window sheet teardown retained DOM nodes, listeners, body resources, and pending async continuations after the owning window closed.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added filtered one-shot window lifecycle listener invokes onDismiss for the sheet's owning window, and close now removes the overlay synchronously while that window is closing, disposing listeners/body resources and resolving the pending sheet interaction instead of retaining them.
cases.evidence: Before this PR, buildMobileSheetShell registered all sheet DOM/window/viewport listeners in a DisposableStore but had no auxiliary-window teardown subscription; the only cleanup path was shell.close(), and callers such as showMobileContentSheet awaited a promise resolved only from close's animation callback. The added regression tests exercise unregister and beforeunload and require the auxiliary dialog/listeners to be released and the pending promise to resolve. blame attributes the base shell lifecycle to a51c7371fac13bbf9413c94ef7a2c6d6711de695.

fixer.title: agentHost: Recover customization sync after reconnect

introducer.title: agenthost: customization syncing data flow

cases.mechanism: The old bundle nonce was derived from mtime and size, so a touch-only update changed the nonce and forced the bundler to delete/rewrite the complete in-memory bundle; the changed nonce then defeated AgentPluginManager's cache and caused a full reverse-RPC fileService.copy to host storage.
cases.symptom: Touching an unchanged customization or skill resource triggered O(total bundle files and bytes) local reads/writes plus a complete remote customization copy, delaying customization publication/session readiness.
cases.fixedBehavior: The PR reads and hashes content after a metadata miss, then reuses the prior bundle and nonce when line 366 finds identical content, preventing both the destructive local rewrite and the downstream remote copy for touch-only changes.
cases.evidence: resolveCustomizationRefs awaits bundler.bundle, AgentCustomizationScope gates its initial resolved state on that result, and AgentPluginManager skips fileService.copy only when the nonce matches. The added touch-only test verifies that the previous result is reused and the in-memory tree is not rewritten. Base line 339 carried the metadata-derived nonce mechanism, and blame identifies its introducing commit.

fixer.title: chat: Keep Mermaid diagrams mounted while a response streams

introducer.title: Add incremental chat rendering experiment

cases.mechanism: Each incremental streaming render replaced the markdown target's entire child tree, detaching an unchanged iframe-backed output code block and forcing its browsing context and renderer to initialize again for successive token batches.
cases.symptom: Iframe-backed Mermaid diagrams repeatedly reload and flicker while a response streams, consuming repeated webview rendering work and often preventing the diagram from finishing before the next update.
cases.fixedBehavior: The target update now reconciles ordinary markdown nodes while retaining reused synchronous code-block elements and their matching ancestors in the live DOM. Streaming updates still reparse/render markdown, but they no longer detach and reload an unchanged contributed code-block webview.
cases.evidence: The base morpher callback at line 182 invoked the full markdown render on each rAF-buffered streaming update. That render targeted the existing chat markdown node, whose base renderer unconditionally reset all target children; meanwhile ChatOutputRendererService mounts contributed code-block output in a webview element under that target. Even though ChatMarkdownContentPart reused the ChatOutputCodeBlockPart object, resetting the ancestor detached the iframe/webview browsing context on every streamed update. The new reconciliation at markdownRenderer.ts:261 preserves the reused output element and its ancestor chain, and the added browser tests prove that repeated append-only updates retain the same iframe contentDocument and create only one rendered output.

fixer.title: test: revert browser-tools HTTP fixture

introducer.title: Remove external DNS dependency from browser tools test

cases.mechanism: The prior remote-test path awaited creation of a localhost tunnel before invoking the browser tool, with no local timeout or cancellation around `workspace.openTunnel`; a failed Windows bind could leave the test blocked until Mocha's 60-second timeout.
cases.symptom: The remote browser-tools integration scenario could spend the full 60-second test timeout waiting for tunnel creation instead of opening the page.
cases.fixedBehavior: The replacement invokes the browser tool directly and removes the local fixture and awaited tunnel setup, eliminating the tunnel-creation wait from the remote path.
cases.evidence: Base line 281 is the awaited `vscode.workspace.openTunnel` call inside the `vscode.env.remoteName` path, and the test has a 60,000 ms timeout. The review context identifies a Windows Remote run where the adjacent-port bind returned EACCES and the promise did not settle. Added line 265 directly invokes the browser tool without tunnel setup. `blame_base_line` resolves the old mechanism to commit 2302cc68e96b866a7e2ece80c9b134d7a3de7ed7.

fixer.title: Fix built-in extensions manifest cache never being hit

introducer.title: #174061 use profile cache folder

cases.mechanism: The cache key comparison includes input.language, but the old cache path included only extension type. The startup window scans system extensions with platform.language while extension-management startup paths scan them with undefined, so callers overwrite the same file with incompatible keys and force repeated full filesystem scans.
cases.symptom: Built-in extension scanning repeatedly misses its cache on the extension-loading startup path, requiring directory enumeration and manifest/NLS reads across the built-in extension set.
cases.fixedBehavior: getCacheFile now derives a language-specific filename, allowing each caller's cache entry to survive and be reused on warm starts.
cases.evidence: ExtensionScannerInput.equals compares language at extensionsScannerService.ts:570; CachedExtensionScanner reads and rewrites the selected file on mismatch; CachedExtensionScanner in the window calls scanSystemExtensions with platform.language, while extensionManagementService startup scanning calls it with no language. The changed filename function separates these entries, and the added tests prove same-language hits and distinct-language files.

fixer.title: dictation: reuse cached Nemotron model after restart

introducer.title: Dictation: download Foundry Local native runtime on demand

cases.mechanism: Across utility-process restarts, stale catalog selection metadata could identify an uncached variant despite a compatible variant already existing in the disk cache, causing the model preparation path to fetch the model again before transcription could start.
cases.symptom: An already-installed, hundreds-of-megabytes dictation model could be downloaded again after restart, consuming network bandwidth and delaying first local transcription.
cases.fixedBehavior: After catalog lookup, the service checks the selected variant first, then scans the model's bounded variant metadata and selects an already-cached variant. The subsequent existing `model.isCached` branch therefore skips the unnecessary network download and proceeds to load the persisted model.
cases.evidence: Before this change, `_ensureModel` trusted only the catalog-selected model's `isCached` value at base line 556 and immediately entered `model.download()` when it was false. The added helper and regression test establish that the selected variant can be uncached while another variant in the same catalog model is already persisted. The local dictation caller states first-use model downloads can be hundreds of MB and transcription cannot begin until model preparation reaches load/session startup. The helper is invoked immediately after the single coalesced `catalog.getModel(modelId)` result and before the download branch.

fixer.title: chat: avoid parsing responses twice for screen reader labels

introducer.title: add table count to chat response's aria label

cases.mechanism: Adding table counting placed a second synchronous full-response Markdown lex in accessibility label generation. Because the accumulated response is reparsed whenever a changed chat row is rendered during streaming, CPU work scaled as two O(response length) parses per render and could block UI updates for long responses.
cases.symptom: Elevated UI-thread CPU and render latency during streaming or rerendering long chat responses, with potential interface/animation stutter.
cases.fixedBehavior: The changed code snapshots the response text once and traverses a single `marked.lexer(responseText)` result to count both table and code tokens, reducing each accessibility-label render from two full-response parses to one while preserving label semantics.
cases.evidence: Base line 145 introduced `marked.lexer(element.response.toString())` for table counting while the same method already lexed the full response again at base line 179 for code-block counting. `Response.updateContent` invalidates the cached string and fires `onDidChangeValue`; `ChatResponseViewModel` and `ChatViewModel` propagate that event, and `ChatWidget` accumulates it then calls `listWidget.refresh()`. The list accessibility renderer calls `getAriaLabel` during row rendering. Thus each visible streamed rerender of an accumulated response performed two synchronous full Markdown lexes on the UI thread. The added test directly asserts one lexer invocation per label after the fix.

fixer.title: agentHost: reduce artifact tool overhead with a prompt experiment

introducer.title: Add tool search to Copilot agent host

cases.mechanism: All server-tool descriptions and schemas were forced eager on each Copilot session launch/resume, so rarely used artifact List/Remove metadata consumed prompt serialization and model-context tokens even when never invoked.
cases.symptom: Unnecessary initial prompt bytes/tokens on artifact-enabled Copilot sessions, increasing request payload and model-context overhead.
cases.fixedBehavior: Artifact List and Remove metadata is excluded from the eager Copilot tool set when tool search is available and loaded through the existing search mechanism only when needed; Add remains eager and unsupported models retain the previous fallback.
cases.evidence: Before this PR, CopilotAgentSession._createServerSdkTools mapped every enabled server tool to `defer: 'never'`; CopilotSessionLauncher calls createServerSdkTools on each launch/resume and includes those definitions in the SDK tool array. Artifact list/remove definitions are only needed when those uncommon operations are requested, yet were therefore loaded into every artifact-enabled Copilot model context. The changed line now maps definitions marked deferLoading to `defer: 'auto'` when the already-established tool-search gate is active, while artifactServerTools marks only List/Remove deferred and leaves Add eager. Tests trace discovery through the existing tool-search client round-trip in both new and restored chats.

fixer.title: menus: Optimize one-shot menu action resolution

introducer.title: Don't listen on menu changed, method 2

cases.mechanism: Every one-shot menu lookup built and tore down event-tracking persistent-menu infrastructure, repeating registry scans, sorting, context-key collection, listener allocation, and disposal on synchronous per-row/per-selection paths.
cases.symptom: Synchronous menu resolution latency and allocation/GC pressure scaled with the number of selected or rendered tree elements and registered menu contributions.
cases.fixedBehavior: One-shot requests now call createMenuActionGroups directly, avoiding persistent-menu listeners, schedulers, dependency collection, and immediate disposal; filtering also occurs before sorting, bounding sort/action construction to contributions matching the current row context.
cases.evidence: The base getMenuActions implementation constructed MenuImpl, called getActions, and immediately disposed it. MenuImpl synchronously constructs MenuInfo, a RunOnceScheduler, a registry listener, disposable stores, and a debounce emitter; MenuInfo scans/sorts registry entries and collects context-key dependencies. Tree-view action resolution calls getMenuActions once for every selected element with a row-specific context, so all of that setup repeated serially per element even though no event could be observed before disposal. The added direct call at line 40 reads/filter/sorts the registry and constructs only the returned actions.

fixer.title: agentHost: Attribute and reduce agent Host turn pre-send latency

introducer.title: inline chat: add experimental Agent Host backend

cases.mechanism: Every non-ephemeral turn synchronously awaited its turn-start checkpoint immediately before provider dispatch. The checkpoint traverses each working directory and runs git status, read-tree, optional git add, and write-tree plus temporary filesystem work, so that entire repository-scaled subprocess chain sat on time-to-first-provider progress.
cases.symptom: Agent Host turns incur avoidable pre-provider latency from a full Git working-tree snapshot, scaling with working directories and changed paths.
cases.fixedBehavior: The capture now starts as soon as working-directory resolution completes and runs concurrently with model selection, attachment resolution, and outgoing contributions; only its residual duration is awaited before provider dispatch.
cases.evidence: Base line 1762 awaited captureTurnStartCheckpoint directly after all other pre-send stages and immediately before setting the provider stage. AgentHostCheckpointService._captureTurnStartCheckpoint calls getRepositoryRoot and captureWorkingTreeAsTree for every working directory; captureWorkingTreeAsTree runs git status, read-tree, optional git add, write-tree, and temporary-directory I/O. The added call at line 1753 starts that same promise earlier while the subsequent selection/attachment/contribution work proceeds, reducing the serialized critical path without changing the before-dispatch invariant.

fixer.title: agentHost: use SDK-enabled reasoning summaries

introducer.title: Adding reasoning summary as exp setting.

cases.mechanism: An experiment-enabled GPT-5.6 session issued a separate `options.update` RPC for reasoning summary after the already-awaited verbosity RPC, serially extending create/resume finalization before session initialization could continue.
cases.symptom: Extra critical-path IPC latency during creation or resumption of experiment-enabled GPT-5.6 sessions.
cases.fixedBehavior: GPT-5.6 finalization now performs only the required medium-verbosity update and leaves reasoning-summary selection to the SDK default, removing one awaited runtime RPC from each affected create or resume launch.
cases.evidence: Base line 805 awaited `session.rpc.options.update({ reasoningSummary })`. `_finalizeSession` was awaited by both `_createSession` and resume paths, and `CopilotAgentSession.initializeSession` awaits `launcher.launch` before registering the SDK event interest or exposing the initialized session. The deleted `_applyGpt56Customizations` called verbosity first and then this reasoning-summary update, so experiment-enabled GPT-5.6 create/resume launches incurred an additional serialized RPC to the Copilot runtime subprocess. The updated create/resume test expectation drops exactly that fourth options update while retaining script-safety, sandbox, and verbosity updates.

fixer.title: mcp: enforce URL policy after variable resolution

introducer.title: mcp: initial work

cases.mechanism: Pending start promises waited exclusively for Running/Error while explicit disposal transitioned the connection to Stopped, so callers and the per-server sequencer could remain blocked indefinitely after policy-driven or user-driven cleanup.
cases.symptom: Stopping or disposing an MCP connection during Starting could leave startup and later sequenced operations waiting forever.
cases.fixedBehavior: The connection now records an explicit stop request and line 156 makes pending state waiters accept Stopped when that request is active, so disposing or stopping a Starting transport releases all queued startup callers instead of retaining an indefinitely blocked critical path.
cases.evidence: In the base revision, start() callers that arrived while a connection was Starting waited only for Running or Error via _waitForState. dispose() then forced the state to Stopped, which was outside those accepted kinds, leaving every pending start promise unresolved; the added tests exercise two concurrent starts and prove both previously vulnerable waiters now settle on stop/dispose. Blame attributes the old wait condition at base line 141 to eb700003ebf3797af1de1f9e222478d6d7f7eea3.

fixer.title: agentHost: avoid recomputing unchanged turn diffs

introducer.title: Show per-turn file changes summary for agent host chat responses

cases.mechanism: Per-request observables depended on the full chat state, so every streamed token update caused each historical request observer to scan chats/history and potentially reparse response edits. Synchronous work scaled with streamed updates times observed historical requests times history lookup length.
cases.symptom: Long Agent Host chats could spend seconds to tens of seconds synchronously processing token streams, causing severe CPU usage and UI responsiveness degradation as history and update count grew.
cases.fixedBehavior: The provider now shares one lazy session/chat source, projects completed turns and the active turn into separate observables at the subscription event boundary, and indexes completed turns by ID only when the history array changes. Active token updates therefore notify only the active-turn path; historical response summaries retain identity and perform no history lookup or edit parsing.
cases.evidence: Before this PR, every rendered request created its own chat-state observable and a derived callback that reacted to every chat subscription change, then walked the chat list/history to locate that request and parsed its response edits. Chat response summaries and timeline entries observe one provider result per request, while streamed token/reasoning actions update the same chat subscription. Thus each token update invalidated all historical request observers and repeated history lookup/parsing; the added regression test at lines 402-450 proves the fixed path now keeps five historical observers at one run across 100 streamed updates, with no additional response/edit reads. The changed projection at lines 301-318 separates completed turns from active-turn updates, and line 317 indexes history once only when the turns array changes.

fixer.title: simplify customization hint

introducer.title: Improve customization message UI and migration behavior

cases.mechanism: Each eligible chat request recomputed disabled MCP migration support by creating a short-lived scope, waiting for its debounced all-server assessment, and disposing it, preventing reuse and delaying agent invocation even though the feature was disabled.
cases.symptom: At least the scope's 50 ms debounce plus MCP support assessment time was added to eligible chat-request preparation whenever migration hints were enabled while the default-disabled MCP migration remained off.
cases.fixedBehavior: computeMigrationHint now checks the MCP migration enablement before scheduling its four-way Promise.all and substitutes an already-resolved empty migration when disabled, removing fresh support-scope creation and the 50 ms debounced MCP assessment from the chat request critical path.
cases.evidence: Base line 73 unconditionally included computeMigration(...McpServers) in computeMigrationHint's Promise.all. ChatService calls computeMigrationHint while collecting every eligible request's context and awaits that Promise.all before preparing variables and invoking the agent (chatServiceImpl.ts:1681-1695,1773-1778). The MCP provider acquires a support scope and awaits waitForMcpServerSupport (agentHostMcpServerMigrationProvider.ts:52-60); a newly acquired scope schedules support assessment behind MCP_SUPPORT_UPDATE_DEBOUNCE_DELAY = 50 and is disposed when the call returns (agentHostMcpServerSupportScope.ts:22,155-215,269-273). MCP migration defaults to false (chat.shared.contribution.ts:2528-2534), and provider-side disabling only skipped createPlan after support resolution, so the old hint path still paid scope creation, debounce, and all-server support assessment despite producing no MCP candidates. The added conditional at line 105 bypasses the provider entirely in that default-disabled case.

fixer.title: Reference hover UI improvements addressing post-merge feedback

introducer.title: sessions: add image previews to reference hovers and align all artifact type behavior better

cases.mechanism: Refreshing an open action-list hover invokes the replacement entry's image content factory as a preservation probe. That factory immediately starts a cancellable fileService.readFile of up to 20 MiB; when the new element is not the one already attached, the pre-fix path discarded it without retaining or disposing its preview handle, so the read and subsequent image allocations could continue for every refresh.
cases.symptom: Live session/reference updates while an image row hover is open can leave rejected preview candidates doing unnecessary filesystem/remote-filesystem I/O and retaining their preview resources until completion.
cases.fixedBehavior: The hover descriptor now exposes disposeContent, and ActionListWidget calls it whenever the factory-created preservation candidate is rejected; the image implementation disposes the candidate and cancels its read immediately.
cases.evidence: The base factory at chatDropdownPill.ts:375 creates createChatPillImagePreview on first invocation, whose implementation starts fileService.readFile with a 20 MiB cap. ActionListWidget.updateItems invokes that factory during preserveHover refreshes, and the new RIGHT line 1699 disposes a candidate when preservePanel is false. The added test verifies the rejected replacement token becomes cancelled. The introducing-line blame resolves to the image-preview change 05ffe98d55ba4d22054b6f18366985bd0180d2dc.

fixer.title: agentHost: fix chat-folder separation review findings

introducer.title: sessions: run Agent Merge per chat folder and present multi-folder sessions

cases.mechanism: The row-height autorun read every chat's `_withDetails`-wrapped workspace, including offscreen rows; observing that wrapper acquires the chat's detailed state subscription, so opening/reconciling a large sessions list eagerly loaded details for all chats.
cases.symptom: Sessions-list height reconciliation caused unnecessary detail subscriptions and host traffic for offscreen chats, increasing list-load work with chat count.
cases.fixedBehavior: The changed autorun reads session/chat workspaces only when `getRelativeTop` confirms the row is fully visible, and sizes offscreen rows without observing workspace details.
cases.evidence: The deleted unconditional workspace reads were inside a loop over every collected chat row. `AdditionalChat.workspace` is wrapped by `_withDetails`, whose observation calls `_acquireDetails()`. The added visibility branch avoids those reads for offscreen rows; `getRelativeTop` returns null outside the fully visible viewport. Blame identifies the base line as introduced by the prior chat-folder presentation change.

fixer.title: build: preserve npm pack errors and retry transient failures

introducer.title: Harden Agent Host E2E and protocol integration tests

cases.mechanism: Repeated failed test-server cleanup left one pending exit listener and Promise closure attached to the still-live ChildProcess per attempt, retaining objects and eventually producing EventEmitter listener growth until the process exited.
cases.symptom: Repeated teardown failures accumulated retained exit listeners/closures on a live test server, causing memory growth and eventual MaxListenersExceededWarning overhead.
cases.fixedBehavior: The changed finally block always detaches stopServer's exit listener on success or failure, bounding retained listeners and Promise closures to one cleanup invocation instead of accumulating across repeated failed teardown attempts.
cases.evidence: In the base implementation, stopServer registered an 'exit' listener but removed it only in the already-exited branch. If descendant capture or killTree failed while the owned server remained alive, the function rejected after its bounded waits while that listener and its pending Promise closure remained attached. The added repeated-failed-cleanup test exercises this exact path three times and asserts listenerCount('exit') returns to zero after each call; the changed finally block now provides that lifecycle guarantee.
